Letter of June 12, 1972, from the State Planner, Washington Office of Program Planning and Fiscal Management, transmitting from four other State agencies comments which are replied to as follows.
Letter of April 25, 1972, from the Director, Washington Department of Eisheries.
<u>Comment:</u> This letter comments mainly on the transfer of State authority to protect endangered species--which is relevant to the proposed legislation rather than the draft environmental statement.
Response: For reply, refer to our comments to the States of Indiana and Nebraska.
<u>Comment</u>: The State comments go on to ask if Federal funds will be provided when authority to regulate and manage an endangered species is returned to the State.
Response: The bill does not provide for a grant-in-aid program and therefore, there is no provision for Federal funding of these activities returned to the State. It should be pointed out that the proposed legislation provides only for the transfer of Federal authority for protection. No other form of management is affected, and the States would retain the authority to carry out other forms of management.
